gaps.note: The seven OP Stack chains with ETH gas have had no network unit in cycles 16 to 21. In cycle 21 only theme units touched them (blind-read probes, ruint lockfile reading). The battery and the targeted set were not rerun at the builds that answer today. Critic query of web3_clientVersion on the networks.json endpoints on 2026-11-25: OP Mainnet op-reth/v2.8.1-72207294, Base reth/v2.5.2-9e380dd/base/v1.5.6, Unichain, Ink and Soneium op-reth/v2.10.0-rc.4-65e80332 (a release candidate in production), Zora conduit-op-reth/v2.5.1-8f0ccac, World Chain world-chain/v2.8.2-9596311. theme-ruint-releases found that Base v1.5.6 links ruint 1.19.0 with the narrow-amount shift fault and checked only the opcode handlers.

L-101 (transient storage reset for deposits) is still open, although the op-reth part can be answered by reading. The critic read op-revm in op-reth v2.10.0-rc.4 (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/op-reth/v2.10.0-rc.4/rust/op-revm/src/handler.rs lines 408-535): a halted deposit after Regolith is redirected to catch_error_failed_deposit, which calls checkpoint_revert to the first checkpoint and then commit_tx. revm-context 43.0.3, the version that release's Cargo.lock pins, clears transient_storage in commit_tx and discard_tx (https://static.crates.io/crates/revm-context/revm-context-43.0.3.crate, src/journal/inner.rs lines 141-158 and 174-192). Base v1.5.6, conduit-op-reth v2.5.1, world-chain v2.8.2, the xlayer and celo builds and mega-evm have their own handler code and were not read for this path.

Celo and X Layer had no network unit in cycle 21. Critic query on 2026-11-25: forno.celo.org reth/v2.2.0-74cc8bb, rpc.xlayer.tech reth/v2.3.0-f60420a/xlayer/v0.0.7. X Layer links ruint 1.18.0, whose overflowing_shl flag is wrong for amounts 64 to 255 (theme-ruint-releases); only the opcode handlers were shown to ignore the flag. L-088 (which hardfork X Layer activated with xlayer-reth v0.0.7.3) is still unanswered.

The Arbitrum family had only theme-go127-arch in cycle 21. Elysium still answers nitro/vlocal+unknown-unknown/linux-amd64/go1.25.12 (critic query 2026-11-25), a build tied to no source, and its results rest on answers alone. Arbitrum One answered linux-arm64 and Robinhood Chain linux-amd64 to the critic query; theme-go127-arch showed Robinhood Chain routes each batch element on its own, so any earlier Robinhood Chain result that relied on one bracket pair is not pinned to an architecture.

Tempo had no network unit in cycle 21, and T14 activates on 8 December 2026 with T15 on 15 December. The custody reading of system_transfer_from (the allowance-free pull for listed precompiles) was done at commit 697ea97, and the endpoint answers tempo/v1.19.1-a9d6748. The critic checked that the list itself is unchanged at a9d6748 and on main (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/a9d6748/crates/precompiles/src/address_registry/mod.rs lines 32-36: FeeManager, StablecoinDEX, TIP20ChannelReserve). The source says pulling only from msg.sender is enforced at each call site and not inside the function (tip20/mod.rs lines 945-958 at a9d6748), and the call sites were not re-read at a9d6748.

Script set 1 did not finish on the QuikNode endpoint, the publicnode reference answered HTTP 403, and the 20 differing set 2 indices were attributed to gas without a per-index gas comparison in this cycle. The publicnode backend reports a different private bor commit each time it is asked: ebcfea01452d (cycle 20 critic), f2a2d63e69f6 (established-l1 this cycle) and bor/a863b8e5cce1/v2.11.1-private/linux-amd64/go1.26.10 (critic query 2026-11-25). None of the three is tied to source, and no battery run was pinned to each commit.

established-l1 reports L-886 as cleared, but its own answer says script sets 1 and 2 ran once against the mixed 48 Club endpoint and were not pinned per build. Only the battery and targeted set were pinned. reth-bsc on publicnode returns an empty log list with no error below block 135,500,000, and no clearance has yet been listed that rests on that endpoint for older ranges.

Assumption T3 (PoolManager transient slots empty at the next transaction) was tested with eth_simulateV1 on 16 networks only. Avalanche, Monad, MegaETH, Arc and HyperEVM have no such method, and on Monad eth_call never runs compiled code (cleared L-674), so the producer path of these five has only source reading (where public) and mined swaps.

The only census that compares every logged outflow of the PoolManager with pool events is the cycle 6 transfer census (research/network-risk/cycles/006/theme-currency-lists.work/raw/census_summary.json). It covered windows of 3 days (Base), 5 days (Robinhood Chain), 14 days (Ethereum, Ink, X Layer) up to 60 days, and full history only on Zora, Celo and Elysium. Nothing mined since then has been checked by that rule. Mined evidence of a usable weakness would show there whatever opcode or system path produced it.

Contradiction: established-l1 files the reth-bsc empty log answer as info and its verifier as low. SCHEMA.md gives low to an operational hazard with no loss path, which the verifier applied; the ledger needs low.

leads.question: Extend the cycle 6 transfer census rule (per transaction and currency: logged outflow from the PoolManager plus ERC-6909 claims minted, minus inflow and claims burned, against the Swap, ModifyLiquidity, Donate and fee collection amounts of that currency) from the PoolManager deployment block to the current head, starting with Base (3 day window), Robinhood Chain (5 days) and the 14 day networks. Before each range, run gapcheck2.py against the log endpoint so that an endpoint that answers old ranges with an empty list (as reth-bsc on publicnode does below block 135,500,000) is not used. Which transactions take a currency out with no pool event or claim burn that pays for it?
leads.why: The organisers say a weakness is usable on at least one network today. A use of it, whatever opcode, precompile or system path it rides on, leaves an outflow that no pool event explains. The only census of that kind covers 3 to 60 days per network and is 15 cycles old.

leads.question: On HyperEVM, Arc, MegaETH, Monad, Avalanche and Elysium, list every mined transaction in which a PoolManager frame of take, settle, settleFor, mint, burn, clear, swap, modifyLiquidity or donate succeeds with no PoolManager unlock frame above it on the call stack, and every transaction in which a PoolManager unlock frame reverts or halts and a later PoolManager frame in the same transaction succeeds. Use callTracer or debug_traceTransaction where an endpoint serves it, on candidates selected from PoolManager logs. Are there any?
leads.why: take and the other delta functions check only IS_UNLOCKED (src/PoolManager.sol:96-99) and the only settlement check is at the end of unlock (src/PoolManager.sol:112). One fault in transient rollback or transient lifetime on the block producing path lets any account take every currency with no settlement. These six networks have no eth_simulateV1, a closed or unpublished producer, or (Monad) compiled code that eth_call never runs, so the probes of cycles 20 and 21 did not reach their producer path.

leads.question: Which Rust-native precompiles and system contracts on Base v1.5.6 (B20 token precompiles), mega-evm v1.7.4 (system contracts and limit accounting) and xlayer v0.0.7 call ruint Shl or Shr with a u64, i64, usize or isize amount that can reach 2^32 or be negative, use the overflowing_shl flag, or convert a signed value with wrapping_from or TryFrom? Grep the crates at the tags that the endpoints report and list each call site with the range its amount can take.
leads.why: theme-ruint-releases showed the 1.18.0 and 1.19.0 faults are off the opcode handler path only. Base links 1.19.0 and X Layer 1.18.0. B20 balances held by the Base PoolManager (OUSD about 5.34 million, F-107) are computed in Rust, so a wrong shift there would change a pooled balance without any EVM opcode being wrong.

leads.question: Do the Tempo precompiles at a9d6748 (tip20/mod.rs, tip20/rewards.rs, stablecoin_dex/mod.rs, tip_fee_manager/amm.rs, tip20_channel_reserve/mod.rs), the Arc native coin precompiles of arc-node v0.8.6 and the HyperEVM read precompiles in nanoreth nb-20261125-2 convert any signed integer to U256 through ruint wrapping_from, saturating_from or the signed TryFrom, which zero extend negative values in every release up to 1.21.1 (faults #701 and #704)? For each site, can the value be negative?
leads.why: The fault is present in every ruint release the networks link, and only opcode handlers were shown not to call it. stablecoin_dex/mod.rs line 2059 at a9d6748 does signed tick arithmetic for prices, and a zero extended negative value in a balance or price path of a pooled precompile token would change balances the PoolManager holds.

leads.question: At tempo a9d6748 and at the T14 release tag, re-read every caller of TIP20Token::system_transfer_from and channel_reserve_transfer. In TIP20ChannelReserve, can an ordinary account open, fund or capture a channel in which the PoolManager is the payer, or make receive_policy_sender differ from the account whose balance moves (tip20/mod.rs lines 997-1010 say it may differ when reserve custody pays a payee), without the PoolManager itself calling the reserve?
leads.why: system_transfer_from pulls TIP-20 tokens with no allowance and leaves the choice of account to each call site. The custody clearance was read at 697ea97, and a call site that accepts a caller-chosen payer would let any account move the PoolManager's stablecoins.

leads.question: Close L-101 for the builds that have their own handler code: Base v1.5.6, conduit-op-reth v2.5.1, world-chain v2.8.2, celo-reth v2.2.0, xlayer v0.0.7 and mega-evm v1.7.4. In each, does a failed or halted deposit revert the journal to the first checkpoint and then call a commit that clears transient storage, as op-revm in op-reth v2.10.0-rc.4 does (handler.rs lines 408-535, revm-context 43.0.3 inner.rs lines 141-158)?
leads.why: Any L1 account can send a deposit, and a deposit that fails still commits its nonce and mint. A handler that commits a failed deposit without the transient clear would carry PoolManager transient slots into the next transaction of the block.

leads.question: The publicnode Polygon endpoint has answered three private bor commits (ebcfea01452d, f2a2d63e69f6, a863b8e5cce1) across cycles 20 and 21. Is any of them a public bor commit, does any differ from v2.11.1 in core/vm, core/state or params, and do the battery and targeted set match when each batch is pinned to one commit by web3_clientVersion brackets? Finish script set 1 there and compare gasUsed for each of the 20 differing set 2 indices.
leads.why: Polygon results this cycle come from a backend whose code changes between calls and is not tied to source, and the gas explanation of the set 2 differences was not checked per index.

leads.question: On the 20 networks other than Ethereum, with pool ids recomputed from the pool keys (cycle 17 used transaction hashes), which pools have a hook address with no code whose bits include 9, 8, 5 or 4, hold liquidity in positions owned by accounts other than the creating account, and have a hook address where code can still be placed by an account other than the creator (an output of a deterministic factory whose initcode takes its owner from tx.origin or leaves an open initializer, or an EIP-7702 capable key)?
leads.why: Positions in such pools cannot be removed (ethereum-reference finding, Hooks.sol callHook needs 32 bytes of return data). Where any account can place the hook code, that account controls the remove and donate callbacks of third-party positions.

leads.question: eth_call on Monad runs the interpreter only (cleared L-674), and block execution runs the PoolManager as compiled x86 code. Which basic blocks of the PoolManager's compiled form at v0.16.5 were executed neither by the cycle 16 compiled-path harness nor by a mined transaction, and do they include signed comparisons (SLT, SGT) whose result is held in CPU flags and consumed by JUMPI, as in the tick bound checks of Pool.modifyLiquidity and the direction branches of Pool.swap?
leads.why: A compiled comparison that disagrees with the interpreter on one operand edge would change which branch the pool math takes in blocks while every eth_call test stays green.

leads.question: In nanoreth nb-20261125-2, how are HyperEVM system transactions executed: the 0x2222...2222 native transfers from HyperCore and the linked contract calls of F-044? For each, is there a separate commit that clears transient storage before the next system or signed transaction, is the journal reverted when the call halts, does a native transfer run recipient code, and is the value debited from a balance that exists in state?
leads.why: These paths run attacker-chosen code ahead of signed transactions in the same block. A missing clear or revert there, or value delivered as CALLVALUE without a debit, would meet the PoolManager's lock flag and native settle (src/PoolManager.sol:353-354).

leads.question: Run gapcheck2.py against every log endpoint that earlier BNB Chain, Ethereum and Polygon censuses used, including the publicnode endpoints. Which clearances and findings (for example the F-091 and F-112 transaction counts and the BNB Chain transfer census) rest on eth_getLogs answers from reth-bsc on publicnode for blocks below 135,500,000 or from any endpoint that returns an empty list without error for old ranges?
leads.why: A census that silently received no logs would clear a network that holds unexplained outflows.

leads.question: When any account calls ArbRetryableTx.redeem for a ticket that another account created, does Nitro run the scheduled redeem with empty transient storage (statedb Prepare or equivalent before it), and is its callvalue taken from the ticket escrow balance in state? Read arbos/tx_processor.go and the block processor at the consensus-v61 commit.
leads.why: A redeem runs right after the caller's transaction and carries a value that native settle credits as msg.value. Earlier cycles tested this rule on eth_call paths only (blind-read verifier lead).

leads.question: To settle F-020 (plausible): does HyperCore require the EVM address that it names as sender of an unsigned spot transfer (AQAv2 treasury, linked contract) to have signed the authorising action, as stated in Hyperliquid documentation or shown by the system transaction decoding in nanoreth? Same fact as L-065.
leads.why: The finding stays plausible on this one link. If the named address must sign, F-020 can be refuted for contracts such as the PoolManager.

leads.question: To settle F-062 (plausible): in the first MegaETH block that reaches the state growth limit, are the transactions skipped from that block included before transactions that arrived later?
leads.why: The specification leaves the order of reconsideration to the sequencer, and the finding's delay claim depends on it.
